local_hypothesis_review: Finite complete projector families and local/ambient inclusion and projection types remain explicit; adjoint identities use self-adjoint projectors.
Positive/nonzero physical and ratio denominators, positive Fourier/Toeplitz orders, exact equal-block divisibility and admissible band width remain stated.
Continuous precision uses a finite nonempty set and positive sensitivities, costs, budget and caps. The maximal clipped endpoint has a unique vector but need not have a unique multiplier.

Mixed-precision propagation uses fixed linear factors and uniform operator certificates. The classical product rounding model remains a separately supplied ordinary real uniform-precision forward bound.
Tree compilation requires finite candidates and additive models. Stability concerns solved scores with strict gaps; local updates use correct unaffected sibling caches.
Support is an inclusion; matrix-power paths are directed walks, inverse reachability includes length zero, and empty graph depth is zero.
Condition-number statements use a nonempty finite space and actual positive square-root normalization. Exact-arithmetic CG convergence remains a separate classical input.

Small-core optimality follows from supplied ordered thin-SVD equations and arbitrary-competitor compression. General SVD existence, numerical QR/SVD implementation and canonical singular-value API identification are outside this release.
Arithmetic/event and pseudo-polynomial table counts are declared models, not instruction traces, physical timing measurements or universal hardware bounds.
classical_inputs: Eckart-Young-Mirsky and associated existence/API boundary: ordered-SVD-data optimality has checked support; general SVD existence is not newly established.
Classical exact-arithmetic conjugate-gradient convergence: formal condition-factor comparison is distinct from the algorithm convergence theorem.
Floating-point product model: exact propagation does not prove IEEE or device-kernel rounding semantics.
Simultaneous spectral decomposition: supplied-projector residual certificates do not constitute an unrestricted discovery algorithm.
